header:
What your card balance
costs you __every year__
footer: Assumes 24% APR and you only pay the interest; work at $20/hr, before tax

vo.text: Five grand? **$1,200** a year. Sixty hours of work.
Ten grand: three full work weeks.
Every $1,000 you owe costs about **$20 a month**.

notes: Stress variant: 14 rows, 4 columns, long two-line labels, silent (no captions, no verdict: the benchmark's winning set-up, so the table may use the caption band), two picks, coral (bad) emphasised column. Maths: interest accrues daily at 24%/365 on a balance kept constant by paying only the interest, so a year costs exactly 24% ($5,000 → $1,200; $10,000 → $2,400); one billing cycle costs 24% × days/365 ≈ 2% (30 days: $98.63 on $5,000, 31 days: $101.92), hence the ≈ on the monthly column. Hours = yearly interest ÷ $20 ($1,200 ÷ 20 = 60 hrs = 1.5 × 40-hr weeks; $2,400 ÷ 20 = 120 hrs = 3 weeks). $1,000 × 2% = $20 a month.
